assumptions: OASF is used as a publication and evaluation-reference surface rather than a complete runtime governance system.
Published records can carry stable references to accountable operators, policies, profiles, and evidence.
prohibitedInferences: Do not infer runtime authority or permitted effect from publication alone.
Do not treat an evaluation report reference as current proof without checking its scope, freshness, and status.
Do not treat an OASF record as a substitute for revocation, audit, redress, or delegated-authority semantics.
comparisonNotes: OASF makes descriptions and evaluations portable; TSMM provides the authority, evidence, and effect semantics needed to assess reliance.
validationHints: Validate accountability, policy, evidence references, and status semantics before relying on an OASF publication.
